question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

**No sooner I reached** the platform than the train left.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The expression "**No sooner**" is used in formal English with the structure "**No sooner had + subject + past participle**."
 
• The sentence has a grammatical error because "**No sooner I reached**" does not follow the correct structure.
 
• The correct structure is "**No sooner had I reached**," which ensures proper subject-verb inversion and tense usage.
 
• Thus, the correct option is **Option 4**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"No sooner had I reached the platform than the train left."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "I had no sooner reached"** – This structure is incorrect because it does not follow the subject-verb inversion required with "No sooner."
 
• **Option 2: "No sooner did I reach"** – While this structure is grammatically correct, it changes the tense from past perfect to simple past, which may not align with the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: "I no sooner reached"** – This option is incorrect because it does not maintain the required inversion structure with "No sooner."
